text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Elevated 502/504 errors on prod-frontend observed in us-east-1 at ~02:34 UTC
alice-eng: I'm seeing a spike to ~6% 502s starting 02:34, p95 latency up too
ben-sre: Confirmed — metrics show failures confined to us-east-1c AZ; other AZs look normal
karen-oncall: paging in. taking incident lead, setting Sev2. creating PD incident INC-2267
mike-infra: ALB access logs show lots of TLS handshake timeouts and early FINs from targets in 1c
laura-prodeng: any deploys around then? nothing in our deploy window
sarah-support: first customer report from Acme Corp: "inference requests timing out" started 02:36 UTC
alice-eng: doing a curl against the ALB from staging host — TCP completes but TLS times out intermittently (handshake stuck)
ben-sre: digging into control plane — cloudtrail shows spikes of `CreateNetworkInterface` 429/Throttling errors in us-east-1c
mike-infra: seeing delayed ENI attachments + `InvalidAttachmentID` in host logs, seems like control-plane attach ops taking minutes
alice-eng: that explains targets flipping healthy->unhealthy quickly
incident-bot: Incident created: "us-east-1c ALB/TLS handshake failures" | severity: SEV2 | owner: karen-oncall
karen-oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain/deregister targets in us-east-1c so ALB shifts traffic 2) open SR with AWS 3) notify customers
laura-prodeng: prepping Route53 weight change to steer traffic away from us-east-1 (we have weighted failover set up)
ben-sre: manual deregistering targets in TG-prod-frontend for 1c now
ben-sre: deregister commands run:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-east-1:123456:targetgroup/tg-prod-frontend/abcd --targets Id=i-0abc1234
```
mike-infra: confirmed deregistered 15/16 targets in 1c, connections draining (max drain 300s)
alice-eng: error rate dropping to ~1.2% after drain, latency improving
sarah-support: posting to status.redwood.com: "Partial service degradation affecting some US users; mitigation in progress"
incident-bot: AWS Service Health indicates EC2 API throttling in us-east-1, SR 987654321 opened by Redwood
mike-infra: AWS support says there's host side maintenance & attach-rate protections in the AZ causing backlog — they're rebalancing capacity
laura-prodeng: customer impact estimate: ~5% of requests over the window, concentrated on customers pinning to us-east-1c or with small AZ affinity
sarah-support: top customers notified via direct message and status updated; support queue flagged P1 for affected accounts
karen-oncall: handing off active lead to ben-sre for sustained mitigation; I'm OOO until 05:00 UTC — ben, you own until then
ben-sre: taking lead. plan: keep traffic off us-east-1, keep targets deregistered, monitor ALB/TLSHandshakeErrors and application latency, coordinate with AWS SR until resolved
ben-sre: created temporary dashboard and muted noisy alarms: https://dashboards.internal/redwood/incident/1809123456
mike-infra: AWS SR update: they're replacing underlying hosts and clearing ENI attach queue; ETA ~90–180 minutes
alice-eng: rolling back a small canary (we had 2% pinned to 1c) and redistributing traffic across other AZs now
sarah-support: customer-facing message (draft): "We've redirected traffic away from the affected AZ and are monitoring recovery; some requests may still see elevated latency. We'll update as resolved."
incident-bot: PagerDuty: escalated to oncall-2 at 03:10 UTC
pagerduty: @ben-sre alerted and acknowledged
ben-sre: TLS handshake metric trending down; ALB error rate continuing to fall
mike-infra: AWS SR updated — host replacements complete, ENI backlog draining, they expect full recovery as attachments complete in next ~30–45m
ben-sre: starting a careful re-register: 3 targets at a time to validate stability
alice-eng: after first 3 re-registrations, no handshake failures observed for 15m
laura-prodeng: moving incident to monitoring; if stable for 20m we'll reduce severity to SEV3
sarah-support: final customer note ready for signoff, includes timeline and mitigation steps
ben-sre: closing actions: AWS SR follow-up + postmortem doc ownership assigned to karen-oncall
karen-oncall: I will write the postmortem and schedule a runbook update for ENI attach throttles
incident-bot: Incident transitioned to monitoring at 04:53 UTC — keep watch for 2 hours
summary: us-east-1c ALB TLS handshake failures, ENI attach throttling caused target flaps and customer impact; mitigated by draining AZ and AWS host replacement
